title: How do they work?
desc: Induction hobs generate a magnetic field that heats the cookware directly, rather than heating the hob itself.

title: What cookware is needed?
desc: You will need cookware made of ferrous metals, such as cast iron or stainless steel, that can be attracted to a magnet.

title: Are they safe?
desc: Yes, induction hobs are generally considered safe because the surface remains cool, and heat is transferred directly to the pan.

title: Are there any downsides?
desc: You might need to buy new cookware, and some users find induction hobs noisy, especially at high temperatures.

title: How long do they last?
desc: With proper maintenance, induction hobs can last between 10 to 15 years.

title: What if I use a non-compatible pan?
desc: If you use a pan that is not compatible, nothing will happen; the hob will not heat the pan unless it has a magnetic base.

title: How do I clean them?
desc: Induction hobs are generally easy to clean. Many models come with a quick clean feature, allowing you to wipe away spills and stains before they set.

title: What cannot be cooked on induction?
desc: Aluminium or aluminium-clad, copper or copper-clad, aluminium foil, glass/ceramic, and some stainless steel products cannot be used (because they will not attract and hold a magnet).

title: Can I leave the induction hob on overnight?
desc: As previously explained, without a pan, there is no heat; you can't leave an induction hob on unintentionally unless you also leave the pan in place.

title: Can we boil eggs on an induction?
desc: Place the eggs in a pot and cover with cold water by an inch. Bring to a gentle boil over medium-high heat. Setting number 6 is good if you're using induction.
